item.title: Presidenta encargada espera que diálogo brinde espacio a todos, incluyendo los que han hecho daño a Venezuela
item.description: La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, afirmó el lunes que espera que las negociaciones con una facción de la oposición ofrezcan un espacio para que todas las voces sean escuchadas; esto ocurre un día después de que la líder opositora María Corina Machado regresara al país.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, afirmó el lunes que espera que las negociaciones con una facción de la oposición ofrezcan un espacio para que todas las voces sean escuchadas; esto ocurre un día después de que la líder opositora María Corina Machado regresara al país. "Espero que el diálogo siga brindando un espacio para la participación política, y que aquellos que han hecho daño a Venezuela —quienes pidieron sanciones y agresiones externas— sientan algo de remordimiento y arrepentimiento", declaró Rodríguez durante una visita a un hospital militar en Caracas. "Espero que tanto el diálogo como el programa para la coexistencia democrática y la paz puedan ofrecer un espacio donde todas las voces sean escuchadas; donde se puedan escuchar aquellas voces que buscan el bien del país", dijo. El regreso de Machado a Venezuela, tras varios intentos fallidos, podría tensar sus vínculos con la administración del presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump. Washington ha señalado que ella tiene pleno derecho a estar en Venezuela, pero, al mismo tiempo, ha elogiado a la presidenta encargada Delcy Rodríguez y respalda un proceso de negociación entre el Gobierno de Rodríguez y grupos opositores que no incluyen al movimiento Vente Venezuela, liderado por Machado. Las conversaciones, que han continuado a lo largo de este mes, contemplan la reestructuración del Consejo Nacional Electoral y del máximo tribunal de justicia, de cara a unas eventuales elecciones.

item.title: ANÁLISIS De vuelta en Venezuela, Machado debe conciliar aspiraciones de sus seguidores y las de EEUU
item.description: María Corina Machado, quien regresó a Venezuela el domingo tras casi un año, se encuentra en una situación delicada, ya que busca impulsar las elecciones que sus seguidores reclaman pero sin entrar en conflicto con el proceso de negociación entre el Gobierno encargado y un sector más amplio de la oposición, respaldado por Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Mayela Armas, Julia Symmes Cobb
item.content:encoded: María Corina Machado, quien regresó a Venezuela el domingo tras casi un año, se encuentra en una situación delicada, ya que busca impulsar las elecciones que sus seguidores reclaman pero sin entrar en conflicto con el proceso de negociación entre el Gobierno encargado y un sector más amplio de la oposición, respaldado por Estados Unidos. El retorno de Machado, tras varios intentos fallidos, podría tensar sus vínculos con el Gobierno de Donald Trump. Sin embargo, Washington, que ha dicho que tiene pleno derecho a estar en Venezuela, también ha elogiado a la presidenta encargada Delcy Rodríguez y ha respaldado un proceso de negociación entre su Gobierno y un sector de la oposición que excluye al movimiento político de Machado, Vente Venezuela. Las conversaciones, que siguieron este mes, consideran reestructurar el Consejo Nacional Electoral y el Tribunal Supremo de Justicia antes de unas eventuales elecciones. Ambos organismos están integrados por leales al oficialismo y además respaldaron a Nicolás Maduro —capturado en enero— en unas controvertidas elecciones presidenciales, a pesar de que los recuentos publicados por el movimiento de Machado mostraban una victoria contundente de su candidato. Los[USN:L6N46B05Q TEXT:" seguidores "]de Machado —decenas de miles de los cuales rodearon su caravana el domingo entre Barquisimeto y Caracas, ondeando banderas, coreando su nombre y entregándole rosarios— anhelan las elecciones y la consideran la próxima presidenta del país. Ella ha planteado que los comicios deberían llevarse a cabo en 2027. El equipo de Machado no respondió de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. Al ser consultada sobre si Machado participaría en las negociaciones, Rodríguez dijo esperar que el diálogo brinde un espacio a quienes abogaron por sanciones contra el país, una crítica que el partido gobernante suele dirigir a la líder opositora. "Espero que tanto el diálogo como el programa para la coexistencia democrática y la paz puedan ofrecer un espacio donde todas las voces sean escuchadas; donde se puedan escuchar aquellas voces que buscan el bien del país", dijo Rodríguez. Aunque Machado ha intentado durante años cultivar una alianza con Trump, el republicano declaró el mes pasado que aún era demasiado pronto para plantear elecciones democráticas. El domingo, Trump dijo desconocer los planes de regreso de Machado, una afirmación que fue cuestionada por una persona al tanto de los movimientos de la líder venezolana. RIESGO DE "CORTOCIRCUITO" CON WASHINGTON El afán de Machado de que haya comicios podría provocar un "cortocircuito" en la relación con Estados Unidos y en el plan de tres fases —estabilización, recuperación y transición— que Washington propone para Venezuela, explicó Ricardo Ríos, director de la consultora de riesgo político Poder y Estrategia. "La idea es celebrar elecciones regionales antes de las presidenciales; es probable que ella presione para obtener garantías electorales y para que las elecciones presidenciales se lleven a cabo lo antes posible", agregó. Pero aún queda mucho por definir antes de que los votantes acudan a las urnas, señaló. "¿Qué garantías tiene el sector gobernante para dejar el poder?", planteó Ríos. "Eso es algo que todavía debe definirse para que esto sea viable; de lo contrario, por muy popular que ella sea, la situación se complica". Que Machado haya vuelto de forma segura fue el resultado directo de las negociaciones, dijo el domingo el secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, añadiendo que espera que todos los actores políticos respalden las conversaciones. La Unión Europea se expresó en el mismo sentido en un comunicado emitido el lunes. Señaló que las autoridades y todos los actores políticos deberían impulsar "un diálogo inclusivo, liderado por venezolanos, hacia la celebración de elecciones libres y justas". "El recibimiento que tuvo ayer (domingo) solo reforzará la tendencia a exigir resultados inmediatos", comentó Phil Gunson, analista senior para la región andina de Crisis Group. "Esto no solo podría provocar una reacción por parte de los sectores más radicales del Gobierno, sino que -en caso de tener éxito- podría derivar en una ruptura política en lugar de una transición pacífica, con garantías postelectorales insuficientes y un país potencialmente ingobernable". El sector opositor que participa en las conversaciones, encabezado por Dinorah Figuera —legisladora elegida en 2015 en el último órgano legislativo venezolano reconocido por Estados Unidos—, calificó el regreso de Machado como un paso significativo dentro del plan estadounidense de tres fases. "Su papel también está asociado a la interpretación de las señales que Estados Unidos ha planteado de reconstrucción y reconciliación. Ella tiene que ser aliada de la negociación", señaló Oswaldo Ramírez, de ORC Consultores. "Hubo un mensaje de Rubio que fue claro (...) No la veo torpedeando la negociación. Ella no puede salirse del rayado".

item.title: New Zealand welcome back eight players but no Savea for November fixtures
item.description: New Zealand will be without injured captain Ardie Savea for their Nations Championship fixtures in November, but will welcome back eight players who had been sidelined with various ailments.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Zealand will be without injured captain Ardie Savea for their Nations Championship fixtures in November, but will welcome back eight players who had been sidelined with various ailments. • Loose forward Savea injured his shoulder in New Zealand's gruelling series loss to South Africa, with flyhalf Ruben Love another of nine players who miss out with injury • Prop Saula Ma'u and first five-eighth Josh Jacomb are two uncapped players who have been called up • Jordie Barrett, Richie Mo'unga, Anton Lienert-Brown, Quinn Tupaea, Ethan Blackadder, Anton Segner, Asafo Aumua and Fehi Fineanganofo all return from various knocks • Loose forwards Leicester Fainga'anuku and Christian Lio-Willie also make a return having been selected by coach Dave Rennie • New Zealand, who top the Southern Hemisphere pool, play Scotland, Wales and England on consecutive weekends from November 7 to complete their Nations Championship fixtures • "This is a really strong squad we have selected. It's great to officially welcome George, Saula, Leicester, Christian, Jamie and Chay back into the squad. item.title: UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide in Gaza after truce
item.description: Israel continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October's US-brokered ceasefire in the enclave, a UN commission said in a report published on Monday that Israel dismissed as part of a "misinformation campaign".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israel continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October's US-brokered ceasefire in the enclave, a UN commission said in a report published on Monday that Israel dismissed as part of a "misinformation campaign". The report by the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel examined violations against Palestinian children since the start of the war between Israel and Hamas on October 7, 2023 up to September this year. It said Israeli authorities had kept committing "genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza", and that the situation had also continued to deteriorate in the occupied West Bank. Another report by the commission in September last year found that Israel had [USN:L2N3V306V TEXT:"committed genocide in Gaza"] and that top Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu incited these acts — accusations that Israel called scandalous. The Israeli mission in Geneva said the latest report was part of a misinformation campaign to demonize the State of Israel. “The attempt to destroy the Jewish state ... continues today through efforts by actors such as the UN Commission of Inquiry to undermine Israel’s legitimacy and deny its fundamental right to exist and defend itself," Ambassador Daniel Meron said in a statement. HEAVY MUNITIONS HIT POPULATED AREAS, COMMISSION SAYS The commission found that Israeli forces continued using heavy munitions, drones, quadcopters, artillery and sniper fire in densely populated areas during the ceasefire in Gaza. It said the [USN:L1N3YO0RL TEXT:""Yellow Line""] which was presented as a temporary ceasefire demarcation, was encroaching increasingly into Gaza, and becoming a de facto border, which the report said reflected Israel’s expanding territorial control of Gaza. Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel's assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel on October 7, 2023. In its report to the UN Security Council, the commission said the situation in the West Bank had also deteriorated sharply, with the number of Palestinians killed in airstrikes increasing from six between 2008 and October 6, 2023, to 254 between October 7, 2023 and September 30, 2026. Commission Chair Srinivasan Muralidhar said the intentional killing of Palestinian civilians and destruction of homes in the West Bank formed part of a broader strategy to exterminate and displace Palestinians. Military operations since January 2025 have led to the largest displacement of Palestinians in the West Bank since 1967, with 34,176 Palestinians remaining displaced as of August 2026, the report said. The commission also faulted the Palestinian Authority, saying it had targeted Palestinians who voice dissenting views and that journalists and human rights defenders had been killed and injured.

item.title: Derrota expressiva de Flávio Bolsonaro torna improvável anulação da eleição, dizem fontes e analistas
item.description: A magnitude da derrota de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) para o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no segundo turno da eleição presidencial de domingo, com o senador ficando mais de 4 milhões de votos atrás, torna improvável que seus esforços para anular a votação tenham sucesso, segundo fontes e analistas.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Simões, Ricardo Brito
item.content:encoded: A magnitude da derrota de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) para o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no segundo turno da eleição presidencial de domingo, com o senador ficando mais de 4 milhões de votos atrás, torna improvável que seus esforços para anular a votação tenham sucesso, segundo fontes e analistas. Flávio seguiu o exemplo de seu pai, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, que está em prisão domiciliar por tentativa de golpe de Estado, ao se recusar a reconhecer a derrota para Lula, que conquistou um quarto mandato histórico. O senador questionou uma decisão tomada no final da tarde do domingo pelo ministro Cristiano Zanin, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), que prorrogou a votação por duas horas devido a alegados problemas no deslocamento de eleitores. O senador afirmou que pediria a anulação da eleição. “É impossível reconhecer o resultado das eleições no contexto que as coisas aconteceram. Vamos pedir a anulação”, disse Flávio a jornalistas após o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) declarar Lula vencedor no domingo. Flávio lembrou que Zanin foi indicado por Lula para o STF. De acordo com três fontes ouvidas pela Reuters, duas do TSE e uma do STF, são remotas as chances de prosperar uma eventual tentativa de anulação das eleições de domingo por parte de Flávio, uma vez que a diferença de votos foi expressiva e o próprio presidente do TSE, Kassio Nunes Marques, já descartou qualquer problema. Nunes Marques foi indicado ao STF por Jair Bolsonaro. Menos de 35 mil votos, ou cerca de 0,03% do total, foram registrados nas duas horas extras de votação determinadas pelo STF, de acordo com uma análise dos registros eleitorais feita pelo professor Pedro Burgos, do Insper. "Do ponto de vista prático considero muito pouco provável que esse pedido seja acolhido. Não diria que é impossível, mas a possibilidade é bastante remota", disse Rubens Beça, mestre e doutor em Direito Constitucional e professor da USP. "Para que a anulação fosse admitida, seria necessário demonstrar, na análise do tribunal, que a quantidade de votos potencialmente afetados pela decisão, nas seções que permaneceram abertas entre 17h e 19h, seria suficiente para alterar o resultado da eleição. Ocorre que a diferença de votos foi expressiva." A petição de Flávio também é enfraquecida pelo fato de que sua campanha também solicitou uma prorrogação da votação devido às fortes chuvas na região sul, de tendência conservadora. A Reuters procurou a defesa da campanha de Flávio no TSE para verificar se vão mesmo tentar anular a votação do segundo turno, mas não obteve resposta de imediato. A recusa do senador em reconhecer a derrota pode desencadear protestos em um país onde a confiança no sistema eleitoral e na independência judicial têm sido abalada nos últimos anos, afirmam observadores. Jair Bolsonaro mergulhou o Brasil em uma profunda crise democrática após a eleição de 2022, quando seus apoiadores invadiram as sedes dos Três Poderes em protesto contra o resultado. Posteriormente, ele foi condenado a 27 anos de prisão por planejar um golpe de Estado. Enquanto Flávio se prepara para eventualmente contestar o resultado, líderes mundiais rapidamente se manifestaram para reconhecer a vitória de Lula, com mensagens de parabéns chegando da União Europeia, do México, da França, do Canadá, da Índia e da Rússia. Presidentes de direita recém-eleitos na Colômbia, no Peru e no Chile também se juntaram ao grupo de líderes que reconheceram os resultados de domingo, mas o governo do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, permaneceu em silêncio. (Reportagem de Oliver Griffin, Luciana Magalhães, Gabriel Araujo, Eduardo Simões e Lisandra Paraguassu, em São Paulo, e Ricardo Brito, em Brasília)

item.title: After return of opposition leader, Venezuela's acting president says hopes dialogue will offer space for all voices
item.description: Venezuela's acting president Delcy Rodriguez said on Monday that she hopes negotiations with a faction of the opposition will offer space for all voices to be heard, a day after opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned to the country.
item.dc:creator: Deisy Buitrago
item.content:encoded: Venezuela's acting president Delcy Rodriguez said on Monday that she hopes negotiations with a faction of the opposition will offer space for all voices to be heard, a day after opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned to the country. “I hope the dialogue continues to provide a space for political participation, and that those who have harmed Venezuela, those who called for sanctions and external aggression, feel some remorse and regret," the acting president said during a visit to a military hospital in Caracas. “I hope both the dialogue and the program for democratic coexistence and peace can provide a space where all voices can be heard, where voices seeking the good of the country can be heard." Machado's return to Venezuela after [USN:L1N45F02O TEXT:"several failed attempts"] risks [USN:L1N42Y0X4 TEXT:"straining her ties"] with US President Donald Trump's administration. Washington has said she has every right to be in Venezuela, but has praised Rodriguez and supports a negotiation process between the Rodriguez government and opposition groups that does not include Machado's Vente Venezuela movement. The talks, which have continued this month, would remake the electoral council and top court ahead of eventual elections.

item.title: Mental health accommodations at work — what employers can ask, expect and change
item.description: Mark S. Goldstein of Reed Smith LLP offers guidance on handling mental health accommodation requests, including recognizing requests, addressing performance concerns and revisiting approved accommodations as business needs evolve.
item.dc:creator: Mark Goldstein
item.content:encoded: Recognizing requests, managing performance and revisiting approved arrangements as business needs evolve. An employee requests remote work as an accommodation for a mental health condition. Another relies on an approved schedule adjustment to manage symptoms, but the employer withdraws it when workplace requirements change. A third is offered a replacement for an existing accommodation and questions whether the alternative adequately meets their disability-related needs. Each situation calls for an individualized assessment. An employee may need an accommodation despite being able to perform the job without it. An approved arrangement may warrant reconsideration as operations change. And a proposed alternative must be evaluated for how effectively it addresses the employee's limitations. Employers have reported a substantial increase in mental health-related accommodation requests in recent years, making these decisions increasingly significant. This article examines the legal landscape and offers practical guidance for recognizing requests, addressing performance concerns and revisiting approved accommodations when business conditions change. RECOGNIZE THE REQUEST WITHOUT REQUIRING LEGAL TERMINOLOGY According to guidance from the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, an employee generally must communicate a need for a workplace change because of a medical condition. The request need not be written or use the terms "ADA" or "reasonable accommodation." A supervisor told that a schedule adjustment is needed for treatment should not wait for a formal application before referring the issue for review. Managers should recognize possible requests, not diagnose employees from behavior. The human resources department can clarify the limitation, the requested adjustment and the connection between them. A request initiates an assessment, not an automatic entitlement to the employee's preferred solution. A symptom-free day is not a disability coverage test. Under Americans with Disabilities Act regulations, an episodic impairment can qualify if it would substantially limit a major life activity when active, and beneficial effects of measures such as medication generally are disregarded when determining disability. Where the disability or accommodation need is not obvious and has not already been adequately documented, reasonable supporting documentation may be appropriate. Keep the inquiry focused on the disability and relevant limitations. An employer generally cannot demand complete medical records or keep requesting information already sufficiently provided. A useful provider inquiry connects a functional limitation to the work. For example, when a provider identifies difficulty processing competing instructions, HR can seek clarification about written priorities or scheduled check-ins. The provider supplies medical information about limitations and effectiveness, while the employer evaluates the job-specific accommodation. Possible mental health accommodations include changes to schedules or breaks, time for treatment, quiet workspaces, written instructions, leave and telework. These are options to evaluate, not automatic entitlements. The inquiry should address how an adjustment responds to this employee's limitations in this job. Keep medical information confidential and separate from ordinary personnel records. Supervisors may receive necessary work restrictions and accommodation instructions, but that does not justify distributing unrelated clinical information. A scheduling manager needs to know the approved hours, not the employee's treatment history. SEPARATE PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS FROM ACCOMMODATION NEEDS The ADA generally does not require eliminating essential functions or lowering production standards applied to employees in the same job. It may, however, require changing how work is performed so an employee can meet those standards. A request raised during performance counseling does not automatically erase warranted prior discipline. The employer should nevertheless evaluate prospective accommodation promptly, rather than treat performance management as a reason not to engage. When assessing subsequent improvement, account for whether an approved adjustment has actually been implemented. The reverse shortcut is also problematic: Satisfactory performance does not necessarily establish that an accommodation is unnecessary. In Tudor v. Whitehall Central School District (2d Cir. 2025), a teacher with post-traumatic stress disorder challenged the denial of an afternoon break after policy and scheduling changes affected earlier arrangements. The district court granted summary judgment because she acknowledged being able to perform her essential functions without the break. The Second Circuit vacated and remanded, holding that this ability did not, by itself, defeat her accommodation claim. Disability, reasonableness and undue-hardship defenses remained available. The decision does not guarantee the requested adjustment, but it cautions against assuming that an employee who keeps working has no continuing accommodation need. WHEN OPERATIONS CHANGE, DISTINGUISH REPLACEMENT FROM WITHDRAWAL Approval is not necessarily the end of the process. Consider a national employer introducing standardized schedules. An employee's approved schedule preserves time for recurring mental health treatment, but the new system would assign conflicting shifts. The company needs to evaluate the effect on that arrangement, not simply rely on the business rationale for standardization. First, identify the actual conflict. Does the schedule create an uncovered essential duty or does it merely require an exception in the new system? Reasonable accommodation can require modifying a workplace policy for an individual without abandoning the policy for everyone. Next, distinguish replacing the arrangement from declining accommodation. EEOC guidance generally permits selection among reasonable, effective alternatives, with consideration of the employee's preference. Choosing an easier or less costly effective option does not necessarily require proving that the original accommodation creates undue hardship. Bourke v. Collins (7th Cir. 2025) illustrates the distinction. Pandemic entrance restrictions disrupted parking and mobility-scooter arrangements for a Department of Veterans Affairs employee. Applying ADA liability standards under the Rehabilitation Act, the court affirmed summary judgment because the offered alternative reasonably accommodated him. It rejected a categorical requirement to prove undue hardship whenever an accommodation changes. The court also noted that, viewing the evidence in the employee's favor, the VA's initial withdrawal without consultation caused an interactive-process breakdown. That alone did not establish liability under the governing circuit law. The practical lesson is to evaluate and discuss an effective replacement, not to cancel first and investigate later. Past flexibility also requires context. In Hayes v. GStek Inc. (5th Cir. May 8, 2026), an Army contractor's information technology employee sought full-time telework for disabilities including depression and social anxiety disorder. The court affirmed judgment on the pleadings, concluding that onsite attendance was essential in that position and temporary pandemic telework had not permanently changed its essential functions. It also found a hybrid arrangement reasonable. Hayes did not involve withdrawal of previously approved full-time disability telework. It is a reminder to examine the actual duties and history, not a general rule against remote work accommodations. In the scheduling example, a different shift might preserve treatment access, but the employer should not assume appointments can move. An alternative must address the relevant limitation. If accommodation in the current job is unavailable, consideration of reassignment to a vacant position for which the employee is qualified may also be necessary. MAKE INDIVIDUALIZED DECISIONS WORKABLE AT SCALE Large employers can centralize review without predetermining the result. HR, legal and operations can establish common staffing requirements and available options. A designated team can then evaluate how those facts affect each employee's limitations and approved arrangement. Where undue hardship is asserted, the ADA regulations require consideration of significant difficulty or expense in context, including the affected facility's resources, the covered employer's overall resources and operational effects. A local budget objection does not end the inquiry. Nor does national head count make employees in specialized roles or different locations interchangeable. Record the relevant change, the options considered and the basis for the selected arrangement. Set an implementation date and a review point, rather than relying on an open-ended approval or an automatic expiration. These are practical controls, not a substitute for the applicable legal analysis. Before rollout, identify affected accommodations, assign responsibility for implementing approved exceptions and establish a way to report problems. Consider interim measures where needed and follow up on effectiveness. An approval recorded in HR's system is of little practical use if scheduling software overrides it or managers assess attendance points against the approved arrangement. Assess overlapping leave rights separately. Eligible employees of covered employers may qualify for Family and Medical Leave Act time off for mental health conditions involving inpatient care or qualifying continuing treatment. Applicable state and local laws may provide additional protections. An ADA determination does not resolve those separate obligations. FINAL THOUGHTS Mental health accommodations call for informed decisions throughout the employment relationship, not just at initial approval. Employers can preserve legitimate performance expectations and operational flexibility while recognizing continuing limitations. The objective is a reasoned, individualized decision and, where accommodation is required, an arrangement that works in practice. The author would like to thank associate Maria G. Arroyo-Poindexter for contributing to this article.

item.title: Votação de Flávio Bolsonaro cresceu no 2º turno em SC
item.description: O candidato derrotado à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) aumentou sua votação em Santa Catarina no segundo turno das eleições, disputado neste domingo, ao contrário do que afirmam publicações nas redes sociais. O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) foi reeleito.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: O candidato derrotado à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) aumentou sua votação em Santa Catarina no segundo turno das eleições, disputado neste domingo, ao contrário do que afirmam publicações nas redes sociais. O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) foi reeleito. Estes são os principais detalhes: “Flávio perde 5,7% e Lula ganha 14% em Santa Catarina. Os números não batem nem a pau!”, dizem posts no Facebook e no Instagram. Dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), porém, apontam que os dois candidatos aumentaram sua votação no Estado. Segundo o TSE, Flávio recebeu 66,65% dos votos válidos (3 milhões) em Santa Catarina no primeiro turno. No segundo, ele teve 69,42% (3,22 milhões). Já Lula alcançou 25,04% dos votos válidos catarinenses no primeiro turno (1,13 milhão). No segundo, o presidente teve 30,58% (1,42 milhão). O PL elegeu o governador, 2 senadores e 7 dos 16 deputados federais do Estado, além de 16 dos 40 deputados estaduais. O PT catarinense conseguiu apenas duas vagas na Câmara dos Deputados e 5 na Assembleia Legislativa. Veredicto: Falso. Tanto Flávio quanto Lula ganharam votos entre o primeiro e o segundo turnos em Santa Catarina. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. item.title: AI capital race sprints into winnowing phase
item.description: Anthropic and Meta are tapping equity markets for up to $195 bln, a third of last year's total issuance. SpaceX also struck a $40 bln chip deal. Giants can lean on their fundraising edge as tighter credit and slipping stocks stymie upstarts. The cost to do so, however, is rising.
item.dc:creator: Karen Kwok
item.content:encoded: Even by the crazed standards of the artificial intelligence boom, $235 billion is a lot of money to earmark in a single day. SpaceX unveiled a $40 billion chip-leasing deal on Monday, Meta Platforms [USN:L3N46C0RK TEXT:"laid out"] plans to raise up to $95 billion of equity and Anthropic released the prospectus for an initial public offering that [USN:L4N42G1FB TEXT:"could fetch"] another $100 billion. Even as credit markets tighten and stocks slip, giants are pushing their fundraising advantage ever harder. The catch is the rising price. So-called neoclouds like CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , which borrow heavily to build servers for AI developers, have experienced [USN:L6N46113K TEXT:"dramatic"] sell-offs in their shares and debt. Yet SpaceX (SPCX.O) , effectively a turbo-charged neocloud, sealed what is the largest-ever financing for GPUs, the most popular chips for crunching chatbot calculations. Meanwhile, Anthropic's and Meta’s plans would equate to roughly one-third of last year's worldwide equity issuance, according to LSEG data. None of this comes cheap. SpaceX, Elon Musk's sprawling satellites-to-social-media conglomerate, has agreed to lease chips acquired by an Apollo Global Management-run (APO.N) vehicle. Its rent formula returns the full financed cost over 20 quarters, plus a fixed rate, meaning the investment shop led by Marc Rowan bears no risk related to the value of the silicon after a five-year lease ends. Although terms are undisclosed, lenders expect to price the deal at interest rates of 7.75% to 8.3%, Semafor reported . The ICE BofA BBB yield index, which reflects companies with a comparable credit rating to SpaceX, has an effective yield of about 6%. At least Musk's enterprise carries an investment-grade rating, meaning it can raise more cash than CoreWeave on the strength of its own finances. SpaceX is also in a stronger position than the leading AI lab. Anthropic, whose credit rating is pending, offered buyout firm Blackstone (BX.N) a yield of more than 10% on junior debt backed by chip lease payments, the Financial Times reported this month. Equity may well get squeezed, too. Meta shares are down 9% since its stock-issuance plans became clear on Wednesday. ChatGPT maker OpenAI has lowered its valuation expectations from a previously mulled $1.5 trillion to a still-frothy $1.25 trillion in discussions over a new funding round, CNBC reported . At base is a vast spending spree. AI capital expenditure could reach $7.6 trillion between 2026 and 2031, for which tech giants like Meta, Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Microsoft (MSFT.O) may issue $420 billion of debt in 2027 alone, Goldman Sachs analysts estimate . The ability to do so should prove a decisive leg-up over smaller rivals. It does nothing, however, to prove the fundamental investment case for AI, even as markets signal exhaustion. The way to bridge the gap: pay more. Follow Karen Kwok on LinkedIn and X . Anthropic on October 26 unveiled its prospectus for an initial public offering that could value the artificial intelligence lab at as much as $2 trillion, Reuters previously reported. Meta Platforms said on the same day that it intends to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising. The Facebook and Instagram owner has initiated public offerings for about $35 billion in common and preferred stock, and filed for a separate at-the-market program to sell non-voting shares worth as much as $60 billion. SpaceX said separately that an affiliate of investment firm Apollo Global Management would buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the billionaire Elon Musk's rockets-to-AI company, in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion. item.title: Average price of gasoline during Trump's term now exceeds Biden's, as midterms loom
item.description: Americans have paid more for their gasoline and diesel at the pump on average during President Donald Trump's second term than they did under his Democratic predecessor, Joe Biden, according to the AAA.
item.dc:creator: Georgina Mccartney
item.content:encoded: Americans have paid more for their gasoline and diesel at the pump on average during President Donald Trump's second term than they did under his Democratic predecessor, Joe Biden, according to the AAA. Surging fuel prices are a major thorn in Trump's side as [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"] loom and the Republican Party looks to defend narrow majorities in both legislative chambers on November 3. The price of a gallon of regular gasoline has averaged $3.472 a gallon since Trump took office almost two years ago, edging out the $3.471-per-gallon average for Biden's term, according to data from the AAA. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Prices for diesel, the fuel that powers the global economy from agriculture and heavy industry to shipping, have also surpassed Biden's national average under Trump, at $4.343 a gallon compared with $4.078 a gallon. US diesel hit a record high on September 22 at $6.523 a gallon as wars in Ukraine and Iran disrupt global fuel supplies. Trump's approval rating fell to a record low this month as Americans worried about high gasoline prices, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll published on October 19. Some 31% of Americans approve of Trump's performance in office, down a percentage point from two weeks earlier and the lowest level in either of his presidential terms, the four-day poll showed. Just 23% of adults polled nationwide approve of his handling of the economy.

item.title: Actor Walter Koenig, 'Star Trek's' plucky Chekov, dies at 90
item.description: Walter Koenig, who brought humor and grit to the role of starship navigator Pavel Chekov on the classic 1960s sci-fi TV series "Star Trek" and seven subsequent feature films, has died at the age of 90.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Walter Koenig, who brought humor and grit to the role of starship navigator Pavel Chekov on the classic 1960s sci-fi TV series "Star Trek" and seven subsequent feature films, has died at the age of 90. "My heart is heavy. Walter Koenig, our Ensign Pavel Chekov, passed away early today," George Takei, who starred alongside Koenig in the show and was a long-time friend, wrote on Facebook on Monday. Koenig died at his home in Los Angeles, the AP reported, citing his talent agent. "Star Trek" creator Gene Roddenberry picked Koenig, who had played only a few prior roles on television, when he decided to add a Russian character to the crew of the fictional Starship Enterprise. The introduction of a Russian officer who worked harmoniously with a racially and culturally diverse crew came amid the real-world Cold War tensions of the era. "We were stating tacitly that peoples of all races and creeds, nationalities could not only co-exist but care for each other deeply, and in doing so we were heralding a future that was very optimistic," Koenig once told a BBC interviewer. While Koenig was the son of Russian Jewish immigrants, he used an inauthentic Russian accent that was sometimes played for laughs. The original TV series ran for three seasons, from 1966 to 1969. Koenig appeared on 36 episodes, and then in seven movies from 1979 to 1994. "I was informed while I was still there at my audition that I had the role," Koenig told the Joplin Globe in 2008. "It seemed like an engagement that might work out over several episodes, but I had no idea that it would totally shape my career and my life." The show remained popular in syndicated reruns and inspired several later TV series and a succession of films. It attracted a devoted worldwide fan base and earned an enduring place in pop culture. Koenig's "Star Trek" fame was a blessing and a curse, as it was for cast mates such as William Shatner (Captain Kirk), Leonard Nimoy (Spock), DeForest Kelley (Dr. McCoy), Nichelle Nichols (Uhura), James Doohan (Scotty) and Takei, who played Lieutenant Sulu. They were often typecast because they were so closely associated with "Star Trek." "Most of the '70s, I didn't work at all, and I blamed it on typecasting," Koenig told the St. Petersburg Times in 1998. He later landed a regular role on the 1990s sci-fi series "Babylon 5" and was an author, script writer and occasional director. Koenig was born on September 14, 1936, raised in New York City and attended the University of California, Los Angeles, before beginning his professional acting career. He suffered a personal tragedy in 2010 when his son, actor Andrew Koenig, took his own life. Koenig married his wife Judy in 1965. They also had a daughter, actress Danielle Koenig.

item.content:encoded: El referencial bursátil brasileño Bovespa se desplomaba el lunes, y la B3 activó el mecanismo denominado "cortocircuito" en los primeros minutos de la sesión bursátil, tras la reelección del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva el día anterior, que contrarió las expectativas del mercado y suscitó preocupación sobre la situación fiscal del país. Hacias las 1400 GMT, el Bovespa (.BVSP) se hundía un 15,9%, a 172.479,84 puntos. En su mínimo, llegó a los 169.516,43 puntos, con las acciones sensibles a las tasas de interés entre las que más caían, como C&A (CEAB3.SA) , que veía un desplome del 50%. B3 activó el "cortocircuito" al inicio de la sesión, suspendiendo durante 30 minutos la negociación de activos al contado, renta fija privada y opciones con acciones como activos subyacentes.

item.title: Safras de inverno da UE sofrem com seca e excesso de chuva, diz Mars
item.description: O desenvolvimento das culturas de inverno na União Europeia está sendo prejudicado pelos solos secos nas regiões oeste e sudeste do bloco, enquanto o excesso de chuva está atrasando os trabalhos de campo nos países bálticos, informou o Mars, serviço de monitoramento de culturas da UE, nesta segunda-feira .
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O desenvolvimento das culturas de inverno na União Europeia está sendo prejudicado pelos solos secos nas regiões oeste e sudeste do bloco, enquanto o excesso de chuva está atrasando os trabalhos de campo nos países bálticos, informou o Mars, serviço de monitoramento de culturas da UE, nesta segunda-feira . "A baixa umidade do solo está prejudicando a emergência da canola e o estabelecimento dos cereais de inverno nas regiões afetadas pela seca, resultando em um desenvolvimento irregular das culturas", afirmou o Mars em seu boletim mensal. O serviço informou que a seca persistente afetou a emergência da canola nos principais países produtores, incluindo França e Alemanha -- os dois maiores produtores de grãos da União Europeia --, levando a um estabelecimento irregular em várias áreas. Esperava-se que os agricultores europeus aumentassem novamente a área plantada com canola para a colheita do próximo ano, incentivados pelos preços elevados, antes que as condições de seca interrompessem o plantio no final do verão. O plantio de cereais de inverno também avançou mais lentamente em partes da França e nos países do Benelux. No entanto, chuvas recentes melhoraram as condições de plantio e o estabelecimento inicial das culturas no sul da Alemanha, informou o Mars. No leste da Alemanha e no oeste da Polônia, o plantio das culturas de inverno progrediu bem, informou o Mars. No entanto, o déficit de chuvas desde setembro reduziu a umidade do solo, gerando preocupações quanto à emergência e ao estabelecimento das culturas antes da dormência de inverno. A escassez de água também limitou o estabelecimento das culturas de inverno nos países do leste e sudeste da UE, incluindo a Romênia, outro grande produtor de grãos. O Mars também reduziu suas previsões de rendimento das culturas de verão da UE para 2026. A produtividade de milho foi estimada em 6,42 toneladas métricas por hectare, abaixo das 6,50 t/ha do mês passado e 9% abaixo da média de cinco anos. A beterraba sacarina foi revisada para 67,2 t/ha, ante 67,4 t/ha, 12% abaixo da média. Prevê-se amplamente que a produção de milho e beterraba sacarina da UE caia para seu nível mais baixo em décadas, após a seca e as ondas de calor recordes deste verão. (Reportagem de Sybille de La Hamaide)

item.title: Russian missile strikes on Ukraine's Kharkiv kill two, injure four, mayor says
item.description: Russian forces launched strikes on Monday on Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, killing two people and injuring four, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said on Telegram.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian forces launched strikes on Monday on Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, killing two people and injuring four, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said on Telegram. Terekhov said there had been three strikes on a city district and that a high-rise apartment block and private homes had been damaged. Regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said Russian forces had launched missiles at the city, a frequent target of attacks about 30 km (18 miles) from the Russian border. In neighbouring Dnipropetrovsk region, Governor Oleksandr Hanzha said Russian forces had launched more than 50 drone and artillery attacks. A drone strike in the city of Pavlohrad killed one person and wounded 10, he said. Three of the injured were seriously hurt.

item.title: ConocoPhillips to reduce workforce in Canada
item.description: ConocoPhillips has informed its staff of a reduction to its workforce in Canada, a spokesperson for the oil and gas producer said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Vallari Srivastava, Katha Kalia
item.content:encoded: ConocoPhillips (COP.N) has informed its staff of a reduction to its workforce in Canada, a spokesperson for the oil and gas producer said on Monday. The reduction includes employees and contractors and is set to take place on Tuesday, the spokesperson added. However, the Houston, Texas-based company did not disclose how many jobs were affected. ConocoPhillips has about 9,900 employees globally, according to its 2025 annual report. "We routinely review our organization to align with our long-term strategy, operate safely and efficiently, and remain well-positioned for future opportunities," the spokesperson said. Last year, ConocoPhillips said it would cut [USN:L6N3W412H TEXT:"20% to 25%"] of its workforce as part of a broader restructuring aimed at streamlining operations and reducing costs following its acquisition of [USN:L4N3HW1E1 TEXT:"Marathon Oil"]. ConocoPhillips said at the time that most of the reductions would be made before 2025 and expected the reorganization to be completed in 2026. Shares of the company were up marginally in afternoon trading.

item.title: Boeing forecast to post small quarterly loss despite recent wins, analysts say
item.description: Despite a flurry of wins for Boeing in recent months, Wall Street analysts expect the planemaker to post a loss per share of 21 cents when it reports its third-quarter results on Tuesday, according to LSEG data.
item.dc:creator: Dan Catchpole
item.content:encoded: Despite a flurry of wins for Boeing (BA.N) in recent months, Wall Street analysts expect the planemaker to post a loss per share of 21 cents when it reports its third-quarter results on Tuesday, according to LSEG data. During the third quarter, the company won the US Navy's sixth-generation F/A-XX fighter contract and certified the last two 737 MAX variants. It delivered 363 737 MAX jets through the first nine months of 2026, its fastest pace ever. Nonetheless, as of market open on Monday, Boeing's share price was down 17.3% year to date. BNP Paribas analyst Matt Akers told Reuters that investors care most about free cash flow and its major driver — deliveries — and current drains — 777-9 certification and building new defense production facilities. While Boeing hit a new record for 737 MAX deliveries, increasing its production rate has taken longer than executives had expected. The company is currently trying to stabilize output at 47 737 jets a month. It has also struggled to increase 787 production from eight jets a month to 10. Boeing's recent successes had already been accounted for by the market, and they had little effect on the company's share price, Akers said. Highlights of investment analysts' consensus expectations, according to LSEG data: $330.5 million in free cash flow in the third quarter, $2.3 billion for the year. $905 million in capital expenditures. Net loss of $153 million, compared to an actual net loss of almost $6 billion during the same period in 2025. Net debt of $25.4 billion, down from $30.4 billion one year ago.

item.title: Now home, Venezuela opposition leader Machado walks tightrope with supporters, Trump
item.description: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, who returned on Sunday after nearly a year away, will walk a tightrope as she seeks the elections her supporters want without running afoul of a US-backed negotiation process between the interim government and other opposition groups.
item.dc:creator: Mayela Armas, Julia Symmes Cobb
item.content:encoded: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, who returned on Sunday after nearly a year away, will walk a tightrope as she seeks the elections her supporters want without running afoul of a US-backed negotiation process between the interim government and other opposition groups. Machado's return to Venezuela after [USN:L1N45F02O TEXT:"several failed attempts"] risks [USN:L1N42Y0X4 TEXT:"straining her ties"] with US President Donald Trump's administration. Washington has said she has every right to be in Venezuela, but has praised acting President Delcy Rodriguez and supports a negotiation process between the Rodriguez government and opposition groups that do not include Machado's Vente Venezuela movement. The talks, which have continued this month, would remake the electoral council and top court ahead of eventual elections. Both bodies are staffed by ruling party loyalists and backed ousted President Nicolas Maduro in a disputed 2024 presidential election, despite tallies published by Machado's movement that showed her candidate had won. The Trump administration captured Maduro in January. Machado supporters, tens of thousands of whom swarmed her caravan between Barquisimeto and Caracas on Sunday, waving flags, chanting her name and festooning her with rosaries, are [USN:L2N46B03Y TEXT:"eager for elections"] and call her the next president. She has said a presidential vote should happen in 2027. Machado's team did not immediately responded to requests for comment. Asked whether Machado would participate in the negotiations, Rodriguez said she hopes the dialogue will lead those who called for sanctions against the country - a common ruling party critique leveled at Machado - to feel remorse. Rodriguez added that the talks offer a chance for all voices to be heard. “I hope both the dialogue and the program for democratic coexistence and peace can provide a space where all voices can be heard, where voices seeking the good of the country can be heard," the acting president said during a visit to a military hospital in Caracas, where she urged politicians to concentrate on serious issues and not putting on a "show". Though Machado [USN:L4N3W51LU TEXT:"cultivated Trump as an ally"] for years, he said last month it was [USN:L1N44V0SA TEXT:"too soon to consider democratic elections."] On Sunday, Trump said he had been unaware of her return plans, though a person briefed on her movements disputed that. RISK OF SHORT CIRCUIT WITH WASHINGTON Machado's eagerness for a vote could "short-circuit" the relationship with the US and its three-phase stabilization, recovery and transition plan for Venezuela, said Ricardo Rios, head of Poder y Estrategia, a political risk consultancy. "The idea (at the negotiations) is to hold a regional election before a presidential election. She will probably push for electoral guarantees and for a presidential election to be held as soon as possible," Rios said. But much remains to be defined before voters cast ballots. “What guarantees does the ruling sector have to leave power (if it is defeated)?" Rios asked. "That still needs to be defined in order to make this viable, because otherwise, no matter how popular she is, it complicates matters." US AND EU URGE DIALOGUE Machado's safe return was a direct outcome of the negotiations, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, a longtime champion of Machado, said on Sunday, adding he expects all political actors to support the talks. The EU echoed that sentiment, saying on Monday authorities and all political actors should advance "an inclusive, Venezuelan-led dialogue towards free and fair elections." "The reception she got yesterday will only reinforce the tendency to demand instant results," said Phil Gunson, senior analyst for the Andes region at the International Crisis Group think tank. "Not only might that provoke a reaction from government hardliners, but it could — if successful — produce a political rupture instead of a peaceful transition, with inadequate post-electoral guarantees and a potentially ungovernable country." The opposition included in the talks, led by Dinorah Figuera, a lawmaker elected in 2015 to the last Venezuelan legislative body recognized by the US, said Machado's return was a significant step in the US plan. “Her role is also tied to how she interprets the signals from the United States, which has called for reconstruction and reconciliation. She has to be an ally in the negotiations," said Oswaldo Ramirez, managing director of ORC Consultores. "Rubio sent a clear message," he added. “I don’t see her trying to torpedo the negotiations. She can’t stray outside the lines.”

item.title: Dollar General overcharged shoppers, FTC and states allege in lawsuit
item.description: Dollar General repeatedly charged more than advertised prices even after receiving tens of thousands of consumer complaints, the US Federal Trade Commission and 20 states alleged in a lawsuit filed on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Jody Godoy
item.content:encoded: Dollar General (DG.N) repeatedly charged more than advertised prices even after receiving tens of thousands of consumer complaints, the US Federal Trade Commission and 20 states alleged in a lawsuit filed on Monday. Dollar General, which appeals to low-income consumers with bargain prices, made millions of dollars by failing to honor prices advertised on fliers and shelves at checkout, the FTC and states allege. The discount retailer's stock was down more than 4% on Monday afternoon. "Dollar General has, for years, repeatedly mislabeled prices, overcharged consumers and failed to correct the issue despite extensive corporate knowledge of the problem," the FTC and states said in a statement. Representatives for Dollar General did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The lawsuit cited numerous complaints from consumers, failed inspections conducted by state authorities, and undercover shopping sprees conducted by the FTC. Portions of the lawsuit detailing the company's knowledge of the practices were largely redacted. California joined the FTC lawsuit along with Florida, Illinois, Michigan, Ohio, North Carolina, Tennessee and 13 other states. Since 2019, Dollar General has paid $6 million in settlements with six states over inaccurate pricing, according to the complaint.

item.title: Soja, café e açúcar caem nas bolsas globais com alta do dólar após eleição no Brasil
item.description: Os contratos futuros de soja negociados na bolsa de Chicago chegaram a cair mais de 2% nesta segunda-feira, enquanto o açúcar e o café também despencaram, pressionados pela desvalorização da moeda brasileira em relação ao dólar, após os resultados das eleições no Brasil.
item.dc:creator: P.J. Huffstutter, May Angel
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de soja negociados na bolsa de Chicago chegaram a cair mais de 2% nesta segunda-feira, enquanto o açúcar e o café também despencaram, pressionados pela desvalorização da moeda brasileira em relação ao dólar, após os resultados das eleições no Brasil. O Brasil é o maior produtor de soja, café e açúcar, enquanto o dólar mais forte frente ao real torna os produtos mais acessíveis para compradores no exterior. A moeda norte-americana mais valorizada também impulsiona vendas de exportadores. O real brasileiro enfraqueceu perto de 12% em relação ao dólar norte-americano no mercado à vista, quando as negociações no Brasil tiveram início nesta segunda-feira, e a bolsa de valores do país suspendeu as negociações por meio de um mecanismo de segurança de interrupção automática, na esteira da reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. O mercado reverteu o otimismo que se instalou entre os investidores quando o rival de direita, Flávio Bolsonaro, liderou o primeiro turno das eleições no início do mês. Operadores afirmaram que a surpreendente reviravolta foi particularmente negativa para os futuros de soja dos EUA, concorrentes do Brasil neste mercado. "Certamente a eleição foi uma surpresa, e isso está ligado à desvalorização da moeda e, consequentemente, à queda nos preços da soja", disse Jack Scoville, vice-presidente e analista de mercado do The Price Futures Group, em Chicago. "A magnitude do movimento nos preços da soja decorre disso e também exerceu alguma pressão indireta sobre o milho." O contrato novembro da soja fechou em baixa de 15,25 centavos, cotado a US$12,4125 por bushel. Os preços da soja também foram pressionados pela chegada da colheita recorde dos EUA ao mercado. Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto negociados na bolsa ICE , considerados uma referência global de preços, recuaram 5,6%, para fechar a 19,10 centavos de dólar por libra-peso. Já os contratos futuros de café arábica na ICE caíram 2,1%, para US$3,0095 por libra-peso, distanciando-se da máxima de seis semanas registrada na quarta-feira, de US$3,1820. O açúcar refinado terminou em queda de 3,6% para US$515,40 a tonelada, enquanto o café robusta perdeu 1,3% para US$3.201 a tonelada. Já o milho negociado em Chicago terminou com leve baixa de 1 centavo, a US$4,55 o bushel, pressionado pelo avanço da colheita nos EUA. O trigo caiu 9 centavos, para US$6,16 o bushel, em meio a uma nova proposta de reabertura segura das exportações de grãos pelo Mar Negro, onde terminais estão limitados por conta da guerra entre Ucrânia e Rússia. (Por P.J. Huffstutter, May Angel e Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: Papa está em condições de realizar viagem à América Latina em novembro, diz Vaticano
item.description: A viagem do papa Leão 14 ao Uruguai, à Argentina e ao Peru seguirá adiante, informou o Vaticano nesta segunda-feira, indicando que a recuperação de Leão após a cirurgia de câncer de pulmão estava ocorrendo conforme o previsto e que ele estava em condições de realizar a viagem de 6 a 17 de novembro.
item.dc:creator: Alvise Armellini
item.content:encoded: A viagem do papa Leão 14 ao Uruguai, à Argentina e ao Peru seguirá adiante, informou o Vaticano nesta segunda-feira, indicando que a recuperação de Leão após a cirurgia de câncer de pulmão estava ocorrendo conforme o previsto e que ele estava em condições de realizar a viagem de 6 a 17 de novembro. O pontífice, de 71 anos, está se recuperando de uma cirurgia realizada em 13 de outubro, na qual os médicos removeram o lobo inferior do pulmão direito e diagnosticaram um adenocarcinoma pulmonar, a forma mais comum de câncer de pulmão. “A recuperação do Santo Padre após a cirurgia continua, e os exames médicos mais recentes atestam sua boa saúde e condição clínica favorável”, afirmou o Vaticano em comunicado, citando o médico pessoal de Leão, Luigi Carbone. “Com base em seu quadro clínico atual, bem como nos exames instrumentais e laboratoriais realizados, não há contraindicações que o impeçam de realizar sua próxima viagem apostólica”, afirmou o comunicado. PAPA RETORNA À REGIÃO QUE BEM CONHECE A viagem de Leão à América do Sul deve ser uma das viagens ao exterior mais intensas realizadas por um líder católico nas últimas décadas. O papa deve percorrer cerca de 31.000 km ao longo da viagem por 10 cidades e proferir 36 discursos. O Vaticano informou que a viagem seguirá adiante sem alterações na agenda divulgada anteriormente. Leão passou décadas como missionário no Peru antes de seu antecessor, Francisco, chamá-lo de volta a Roma em 2023 e promovê-lo a cargos no Vaticano. A viagem, portanto, marcará uma espécie de volta ao lar para o primeiro pontífice norte-americano. “Estou ansioso para retornar ao continente onde vivi tantos momentos da minha vida”, disse ele na mensagem do Vaticano. “Que esta viagem seja uma ocasião para abrirmos nossos corações uns aos outros, fortalecermos nossa comunhão como irmãos e irmãs e renovarmos nosso compromisso de proclamar o Evangelho com alegria”, disse Leão. Em seu comunicado, o Vaticano informou que Leão estava “ajustando sua agenda diária em consulta com seus médicos para priorizar sua recuperação, ao mesmo tempo em que continua a cumprir as responsabilidades de seu ministério”. No domingo, o papa dirigiu-se aos fiéis na Praça de São Pedro, mas, por recomendação médica, cancelou uma visita de um dia à cidade de Assis, no centro da Itália, que estava marcada para terça-feira.

item.title: Microsoft offers buyouts to around 60,000 employees to contain costs
item.description: Microsoft said on Monday it is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, or more than a quarter of its global workforce, as the technology giant looks to contain costs and help fund its massive AI investments.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: Microsoft (MSFT.O) said on Monday it is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, or more than a quarter of its global workforce, as the technology giant looks to contain costs and help fund its massive AI investments. Staffers across the Windows maker would be eligible for the offers, including those working in AI experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox and Windows + Devices, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters, requesting anonymity as the matter was private. Units such as marketing, commercial business and security will be excluded, the source added. "This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs," Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said in a staff memo. Like other tech giants, Microsoft is spending hundreds of billions of dollars on AI data centers and chips, drawing scrutiny from investors over whether the returns will justify the staggering cost. The company, slated to report first-quarter results after markets close on Wednesday, has forecast $175 billion in capital expenditures for the 2026 calendar year. Microsoft had 223,000 full-time employees globally as of June 30, 2026, according to its annual filing. Shares of Microsoft, which had risen about 10% this year, were up about 1% on Monday. The development was first reported by Business Insider. The company earlier this year offered voluntary buyouts to about 7% of its US workforce, or about 9,000 employees. In July, Microsoft [USN:L4N4380XC TEXT:"announced it would cut 4,800 jobs"], or about 2.1% of its global workforce, overhauling its Xbox gaming business and divesting up to five studios as it looks to boost returns after years of heavy investment in the division. "This offer will be available to eligible employees in participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States at level 70 and below," Microsoft said on Monday. The company said it was a time-limited, voluntary program and built on insights gained from a previous voluntary retirement program. The eligible employees will receive details within the next few hours, it added.

item.title: Colombia lanza emisión de bonos globales en dólares a cinco, 10 y 30 años: IFR
item.description: El Gobierno de Colombia lanzó el lunes una emisión de bonos globales en dólares a cinco, 10 y 30 años, según un reporte de IFR, un servicio de información financiera de LSEG.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno de Colombia lanzó el lunes una emisión de bonos globales en dólares a cinco, 10 y 30 años, según un reporte de IFR, un servicio de información financiera de LSEG. Las emisiones tienen como propósito financiar el presupuesto de gastos del país sudamericano, aunque no se informó inmediatamente si se utilizarán para cubrir necesidades de este año o para prefinanciar el 2027. Los vencimientos están propuestos para 2032, 2037 y 2056, agregó el artículo. IFR precisó que los bonos a 5 años tienen una tasa guía de 7,10%, a 10 años un 7,70% y a 30 años entre un 8,15% y 8,25%. Según agentes del mercado, el Gobierno busca emitir alrededor de 5.000 millones de dólares. Los agentes colocadores de la operación son BBVA, Itaú y JP Morgan. Colombia ya había finalizado sus necesidades de financiamiento de este año vía bonos internacionales, aunque la semana pasada anunció un recorte de 13,8 billones de pesos (4.326 millones de dólares) en el presupuesto, inferior a los 21,9 billones de pesos que pretendía reducir, lo que supondría necesidad de más recursos. El presupuesto de 2027 propone colocaciones de deuda pública interna por 150,9 billones de pesos y endeudamiento externo por unos 26.101 millones de dólares vía emisiones en el mercado internacional de capitales y préstamos con los bancos de desarrollo multilaterales y bilaterales. El presidente De La Espriella anunció que en los próximos días radicará ante el Congreso la denominada “Ley de Rescate Económico”, una iniciativa con la que el Gobierno busca enfrentar los desequilibrios fiscales y presupuestales del próximo año.

item.title: Rendimiento de bonos Tesoro EEUU a 10 años cotiza estable, a la espera de la Fed
item.description: El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro a 10 años cotizó estable el lunes, mientras el mercado espera los resultados de las principales empresas de inteligencia artificial (IA) esta semana y antes de la reunión de la Reserva Federal, que se prevé que haga una pausa en sus alzas de las tasas de interés.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro a 10 años cotizó estable el lunes, mientras el mercado espera los resultados de las principales empresas de inteligencia artificial (IA) esta semana y antes de la reunión de la Reserva Federal, que se prevé que haga una pausa en sus alzas de las tasas de interés. La presentación el lunes por parte de la empresa de IA Anthropic de la documentación para su oferta pública inicial (OPI) impulsó las acciones, y la IA seguirá siendo el centro de atención con las publicaciones de resultados de Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) y Amazon.com (AMZN.O) durante la semana. Los rendimientos de los bonos a 10 años se mantuvo en menos del 5%. El jueves pasado, el bono de referencia había anotado su mayor caída diaria de casi cuatro años, en un contexto de desplome las bolsas provocada por el temor sobre la sostenibilidad de la demanda de IA. "La semana pasada hubo mucha volatilidad", dijo Jim Barnes, director de renta fija de Bryn Mawr Trust. Los inversores quieren escuchar lo que digan esta semana las empresas relacionadas con la IA para hacerse una idea del gasto futuro, pero también de las perspectivas económicas generales, añadió. "Esto está empezando a influir en las expectativas de los inversores respecto a los rendimientos de los bonos en el futuro", añadió. Los inversores también estarán pendientes de la Fed, de la que se espera que mantenga las tasas de interés sin cambios cuando anuncie su decisión de política monetaria el miércoles. Las expectativas del mercado de un alza de tasas han bajado recientemente, en la medida en que los rendimientos se han moderado y los datos económicos han sido dispares. Los futuros sobre tasas de interés descontaban el lunes una probabilidad del 90% de que se mantengan las tasas sin cambios en la reunión de la Fed de esta semana, según CME FedWatch. El rendimiento del bono del Tesoro a 10 años de referencia cotizaba casi sin cambios en 4,988%, mientras que el de 30 años perdía 1,5 puntos básicos, al 5,3%. El retorno a dos años , que suele evolucionar en consonancia con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, caía 1,5 puntos básicos, al 4,714%. Una parte de la curva de rendimientos que mide la diferencia entre los rendimientos de los bonos a 2 y a 10 años , y que se considera un indicador de las expectativas económicas, se situó en 27,2 puntos básicos positivos. El diferencial se redujo a un mínimo de casi un mes.

item.title: CEO da Petrobras vê queda das ações após vitória de Lula como especulativa
item.description: A presidente da Petrobras , Magda Chambriard, afirmou nesta segunda-feira que a forte queda nas ações da estatal após a reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva foi um "movimento especulativo" e não reflete os fundamentos da empresa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A presidente da Petrobras (PETR3.SA) , Magda Chambriard, afirmou nesta segunda-feira que a forte queda nas ações da estatal após a reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva foi um "movimento especulativo" e não reflete os fundamentos da empresa. Em entrevista à Reuters, Chambriard disse que a Petrobras continua sendo uma empresa sólida, com uma forte carteira de investimentos, e que não se deixará influenciar por movimentos de curto prazo do mercado. "A hora é de comprar (ações). Infelizmente não posso", disse a executiva. As ações da Petrobras negociadas na B3 caíam cerca de 10% nesta segunda-feira após o presidente Lula derrotar o senador Flávio Bolsonaro no segundo turno das eleições de domingo, contrariando as pesquisas e garantindo um quarto mandato não consecutivo.

item.title: Datagro vê queda de 5% na produção de açúcar do centro-sul em 26/27 e alta de 10,4% para etanol
item.description: A produção de açúcar do centro-sul do Brasil 2026/27 (abril/março) deverá atingir 38,42 milhões de toneladas, uma queda de 5% no comparativo com o ciclo anterior, por conta de impactos do El Niño e de uma redução na alocação de cana-de-açúcar para a fabricação do adoçante, estimou nesta segunda-feira a consultoria Datagro.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Samora
item.content:encoded: A produção de açúcar do centro-sul do Brasil 2026/27 (abril/março) deverá atingir 38,42 milhões de toneladas, uma queda de 5% no comparativo com o ciclo anterior, por conta de impactos do El Niño e de uma redução na alocação de cana-de-açúcar para a fabricação do adoçante, estimou nesta segunda-feira a consultoria Datagro. De outro lado, a fabricação total de etanol (de cana e milho) foi estimada em 37,2 bilhões de litros, avanço de 10,4%, com a expansão do setor de etanol de milho e também maior "mix" de cana para o biocombustível. As projeções de açúcar e etanol indicam volumes menores em relação à perspectiva divulgada em maio pela Datagro, quando as chuvas associadas ao El Niño ainda não haviam afetado os trabalhos de moagem. Naquele mês, a Datagro projetava [USN:L1N41Q0MU TEXT:"40,98 milhões"] de toneladas de açúcar, enquanto a de etanol era vista em 38,61 bilhões de litros. A estimativa de safra de cana do centro-sul, por outro lado, indica um crescimento de 4,8% no comparativo com o ciclo passado, para 640,5 milhões de toneladas, mas uma leve queda na comparação com a projeção de maio (642,2 milhões de toneladas). Durante a apresentação em evento da consultoria, o presidente da Datagro, Plinio Nastari, citou que as chuvas atrapalharam a colheita e a moagem no centro-sul, principal região produtora de açúcar do mundo. Ele estimou 28,6 dias perdidos pelas precipitações, versus média histórica de 13,6 dias. Essa perda é equivalente a cerca de 50 milhões de toneladas de cana que não foi processada, disse o consultor. "Muitas usinas projetam levar a moagem de cana até a segunda quinzena de dezembro", disse Nastari, observando que os trabalhos deverão ser alongados, numa tentativa de minimizar a perda pelas chuvas. Contudo, a Datagro ainda estima 34 milhões de toneladas de cana bisada em 31 de março de 2027, volume que deverá ser processado no ano que vem. O especialista disse que ainda é cedo para estimar o tamanho da safra 2027/28 no maior produtor global de açúcar, lembrando que é preciso acompanhar o clima e os preços das commodities. Até 1º de outubro, a moagem no centro-sul havia somado 482,3 milhões de toneladas, queda de 1,6% no comparativo anual, segundo dados compilados pelo Ministério da Agricultura citados pelo especialista. Segundo ele, o aumento do consumo de etanol no Brasil e o impacto do El Niño levaram a um aumento dos preços, ainda que as subvenções à gasolina e o controle de preços pela Petrobras impeçam um avanço ainda maior da demanda do biocombustível, em momento em que os preços do petróleo dispararam devido à guerra no Irã. O "mix" de produção de cana para açúcar em 2026/27 deve cair para 46,7%, ante 50,4% no ciclo passado. Já a produção de etanol de milho em 2026/27 deverá crescer 10,4% no comparativo anual, para 10,15 bilhões de litros, um crescimento abaixo do previsto inicialmente, disse Nastari. ESTOQUES GLOBAIS O mercado global de açúcar no ano mundial 2026/27 (outubro/setembro) deverá ser deficitário em 3,92 milhões de toneladas (açúcar bruto equivalente), estimou a Datagro, ante um superávit de 730 mil toneladas no ciclo passado. Essa redução acontece em meio a uma queda de cerca de 4 milhões de toneladas na produção de açúcar branco da União Europeia, para 12,7 milhões de toneladas, em 2026/27, devido à queda na área plantada. "A União Europeia deve se voltar para maiores importações em 2026/27, com o volume podendo chegar a 3 milhões de toneladas", disse Nastari. Ele vê uma estagnação no consumo global, o que tem impactado embarques do Brasil, que estão enfraquecidos. Essa situação acontece diante do aumento da produção da China para patamares acima de 13 milhões de toneladas em 2025/26 e em 2026/27, versus 11 milhões em 2024/25. "As importações (da China) em 2026/27 devem cair para 2,7 milhões de toneladas, metade do volume de 21/22", afirmou.

item.title: 'No fuel to keep babies warm': shortages push hospitals in Yemen's Taiz to brink
item.description: Fuel shortages in Yemen's besieged city of Taiz have forced one hospital to cut the number of incubators it can operate from 40 to 10, putting newborn babies at risk as weeks of fighting choke off vital supplies and deepen a humanitarian crisis affecting hundreds of thousands of people.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
item.content:encoded: Fuel shortages in Yemen's besieged city of [USN:L8N46125M TEXT:"Taiz"] have forced one hospital to cut the number of incubators it can operate from 40 to 10, putting newborn babies at risk as weeks of fighting choke off vital supplies and deepen a humanitarian crisis affecting hundreds of thousands of people. "There's no oxygen, there's no fuel to run the incubators, to keep the babies warm," said Nada Ahmed, a nurse in the neonatal unit of the Yemeni-Swedish Hospital for Maternity and Childhood. Nawal Najeeb, a supervisor in the neonatal unit, warned the facility could be forced to halt operations if fuel supplies do not arrive. "It will be a catastrophe for the babies, a catastrophe of deaths and disabilities." Taiz has been largely isolated since October 3, with fighting[USN:L6N4670EA TEXT:" preventing humanitarian supplies"] from entering and civilians from leaving, following an escalation in clashes between the Saudi-backed government and the Iran-aligned Houthi movement. FUEL PRICES SURGE Key supply routes, including the Taiz-Aden corridor, have been blocked by Houthi forces, worsening shortages of water, food and fuel. The city hosts nearly half of the 250,000 people displaced by the latest fighting, according to the United Nations. In Taiz city, 42 health facilities are reporting acute shortages of fuel, oxygen, medicines and medical supplies, WHO spokesperson Christian Lindmeier said. Fuel prices have surged to 2,000 Yemeni rials per litre, driver Abdullah al-Radfani told Reuters. Oxfam Yemen's policy, advocacy and media manager, Fatma Jaffar Shotah, described one dialysis patient who has to spend two nights at a healthcare centre rather than travelling home between sessions because regular journeys have become unaffordable, the cost rising from half a dollar to around $10. "Fuel shortage inside the city is having catastrophic impacts on people's lives," she said. The strain is being felt beyond Taiz. Aid group Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said fuel shortages were causing power outages at hospitals and primary healthcare centres in the southern governorates of Aden and Lahj, affecting operating theatres and intensive care units. HUNGER AND MALNUTRITION UN agencies and aid groups also warned of worsening hunger and malnutrition. The World Food Programme says that more than 800,000 people have been cut off from food assistance in Taiz and surrounding areas. UNICEF spokesperson Ricardo Pires said 52,000 of the 168,000 children screened in Taiz so far this year are acutely malnourished, including more than 11,500 suffering from severe acute malnutrition. Although UNICEF has put in place nearly 8,000 cartons of life-saving therapeutic food, enough to sustain treatment services for around three months, Pires warned that worsening insecurity and movement restrictions could hamper future deliveries and prevent families from reaching treatment centres. MSF said growing displacement was aggravating child malnutrition in southern Yemen, an area which has already faced a long-standing hunger crisis, as families flee fighting in the north and along the west coast. Between September 15 and October 22, MSF screened 299 children under 5 at its mobile clinics in Aden and Lahj. Forty-four children, or 14.7%, were suffering from moderate acute malnutrition, while 28 children, or 9.4%, were severely malnourished and in need of hospital care. "In each location we go, on a daily basis, we see at least one or two children who are in severe acute malnutrition," said MSF's mobile health activity manager, Sara Ghanem.

item.title: Wall Street cierra en alza ya que solicitud de OPI de Anthropic impulsa acciones de IA
item.description: Wall Street avanzó el lunes, y tanto el S&P 500 como el Nasdaq se recuperaron tras anotar caídas semanales consecutivas, ya que la solicitud de una oferta pública inicial (OPI) de Anthropic impulsó el optimismo en torno a las acciones relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial (IA).
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: Wall Street avanzó el lunes, y tanto el S&P 500 como el Nasdaq se recuperaron tras anotar caídas semanales consecutivas, ya que la solicitud de una oferta pública inicial (OPI) de Anthropic impulsó el optimismo en torno a las acciones relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial (IA). Anthropic reveló pérdidas considerables y un crecimiento vertiginoso de los ingresos en su solicitud de salida a bolsa en Estados Unidos, en la que expuso su ambición de crear sistemas de inteligencia artificial capaces de transformar la economía mundial a pesar de los altos costos que conlleva el desarrollo de la tecnología. El laboratorio de IA sigue adelante con sus planes de salida a bolsa a pesar de que el calendario de ofertas, que en otoño boreal solía estar repleto, se ha reducido, ya que la volatilidad del mercado ha llevado a las empresas a retrasar sus ofertas. La presentación de Anthropic se produce en un momento en que los inversores analizan con mayor detenimiento el posible retorno de las inversiones masivas en IA, justo al inicio de una semana intensa. Entre los eventos clave destacan el comunicado de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal el miércoles, los datos sobre crecimiento económico e inflación el jueves, y una serie de informes de resultados corporativos. Más de un tercio de las empresas que integran el índice S&P 500 tienen previsto presentar sus resultados esta semana, incluidas las grandes compañías tecnológicas Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) y Amazon.com (AMZN.O) . Sus cifras serán examinadas minuciosamente en busca de señales que indiquen si las cuantiosas inversiones en IA se están traduciendo efectivamente en crecimiento. Según datos preliminares, el S&P 500 (.SPX) subió 53,35 puntos, O un 0,70%, a 7.677,03 unidades; el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) ganó 214,02 puntos, o un 0,83%, a 26.169,38 unidades; y el Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) sumó 146,60 puntos, o un 0,28%, a 52.361,76 unidades. Las firmas de semiconductores y chips, consideradas por muchos como algunas de las grandes beneficiadas del auge de la IA, contribuyeron a impulsar las subidas. El índice general de chips de Filadelfia (.SOX) escaló cera de un 3% en la sesión, aunque acumula una baja del 12% en el mes.
